Main.sentence: African Americans , also known as Black Americans and formerly called Afro-Americans , are an ___E:American racial and ethnic group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_and_ethnicity_in_the_United_States)___ who as defined by the ___E:United States census U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_census)___ , consists of ___E:Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americans)___ who have ancestry from "any of the ___E:Black U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_people)___ racial groups of ___E:Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa)___ ".
African Americans constitute the second largest racial and ethnic group in the U.S. after ___E:White Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Americans)___ .
The term "African American" generally denotes descendants of ___E:Africans enslaved in the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_in_the_United_States)___ .

According to annual estimates from the ___E:U.S. Census Bureau U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau)___ , as of July 1, 2024, the Black population was estimated at 42,951,595, representing approximately 12.63% of the total ___E:U.S. population U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographics_of_the_United_States)___ .

___E:African-American history U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_history)___ began in the 16th century, when ___E:African slave traders U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_in_Africa)___ sold African artisans, farmers, and warriors to ___E:European slave traders U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_slave_trade)___ , who ___E:transported them across the Atlantic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Passage)___ to ___E:the Western Hemisphere U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_in_the_colonial_history_of_the_United_States)___ .

They were ___E:sold as slaves U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_in_the_colonial_history_of_the_United_States)___ to European colonists and put to work on ___E:plantations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plantation)___ , particularly ___E:in the southern colonies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plantation_complexes_in_the_Southern_United_States)___ .

A few were able to achieve freedom through ___E:manumission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manumission)___ or escape, and founded independent communities before and during the ___E:American Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolution)___ .

After the United States was founded in 1783, most ___E:Black people continued to be enslaved U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_in_the_United_States)___ , primarily concentrated in the ___E:American South U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_United_States)___ , with four million enslaved people only ___E:liberated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution)___ with the ___E:Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War)___ in 1865.

During ___E:Reconstruction U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reconstruction_Era)___ , African Americans gained ___E:citizenship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution)___ and adult-males the ___E:right to vote U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution)___ ; however, due to widespread ___E:White supremacy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_supremacy_in_the_United_States)___ , they were treated as ___E:second-class citizens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second-class_citizen)___ and soon ___E:disenfranchised in the South U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disfranchisement_after_the_Reconstruction_era)___ .

These circumstances changed due to participation in the ___E:military conflicts of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_African_Americans)___ , substantial ___E:migration out of the South U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Migration_(African_American))___ , the elimination of legal ___E:racial segregation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_segregation_in_the_United_States)___ , and the ___E:civil rights movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_rights_movement)___ which sought political and social freedom.

However, ___E:racism against African Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racism_against_African_Americans)___ and ___E:racial socioeconomic disparity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_inequality_in_the_United_States)___ remain a problem into the 21st century.
In the 20th and 21st centuries, immigration has played an increasingly significant role in the African-American community.
As of 2022, 10% of the U.S.
Black population were immigrants, and 20% were either immigrants or the children of immigrants.
While some Black immigrants or their children may also come to identify as African American, the majority of first-generation immigrants do not, preferring to identify with their nation of origin.

Most African Americans are of ___E:West African U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Africa)___ and coastal ___E:Central African U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Africa)___ ancestry, with varying amounts of ___E:Western European U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Europe)___ and ___E:Native American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States)___ ancestry.

___E:African-American culture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_culture)___ has had a significant influence on worldwide culture, making numerous contributions to ___E:visual arts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_art)___ , ___E:literature U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_literature)___ , the English language, ___E:philosophy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africana_philosophy)___ , politics, ___E:cuisine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_food)___ , ___E:sports U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans_in_sports)___ , and ___E:music U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_music)___ .

The African-American contribution to popular music is so profound that most ___E:American music U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_the_United_States)___ , including ___E:jazz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz)___ , ___E:gospel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_music)___ , ___E:blues U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blues)___ , ___E:rock and roll U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll)___ , ___E:funk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funk)___ , ___E:disco U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disco)___ , ___E:house U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_music)___ , ___E:techno U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Techno)___ , ___E:hip hop U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop_music)___ , ___E:R&B U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_and_blues)___ , ___E:trap U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trap_music)___ , and ___E:soul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music)___ , has its origins either partially or entirely in the African-American community.

The vast majority of those who were enslaved and transported in the ___E:transatlantic slave trade U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_slave_trade)___ were people from several ___E:Central U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Africa)___ and ___E:West African U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Africa)___ ethnic groups.

They had been captured directly by European slave traders in coastal raids,  or sold by West African slave traders, or by half-European "merchant princes"  to European slave traders, who brought them to the Americas.
The first African slaves in what is now the United States arrived in the early 16th century.

Africans were among ___E:Juan Ponce de León U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Ponce_de_Le%C3%B3n)___ 's 1513 voyage that landed in what would become ___E:Spanish Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Florida)___ , and enslaved Africans arrived around the same time to ___E:Spanish Puerto Rico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_settlement_of_Puerto_Rico)___ .

Africans also came via ___E:Santo Domingo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captaincy_General_of_Santo_Domingo)___ in the ___E:Caribbean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean)___ to the ___E:San Miguel de Gualdape U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Miguel_de_Gualdape)___ colony (most likely located in the ___E:Winyah Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winyah_Bay)___ area of present-day ___E:South Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina)___ ), founded by Spanish explorer ___E:Lucas Vázquez de Ayllón U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_V%C3%A1zquez_de_Ayll%C3%B3n)___ in 1526.  The ill-fated colony was almost immediately disrupted by a fight over leadership, during which the slaves revolted and fled the colony to seek refuge among local ___E:Native Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_the_Americas)___ .
De Ayllón and many of the colonists died shortly afterward, due to an epidemic and the colony was abandoned.
The settlers and the slaves who had not escaped returned to the Island of ___E:Hispaniola U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispaniola)___ , whence they had come.

The enslaved explorer ___E:Esteban U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estevanico)___ arrived in Florida with the ___E:Narváez expedition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narv%C3%A1ez_expedition)___ in 1528, a journey that first landed in Santo Domingo and later traveled into ___E:Spanish Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Texas)___ and the ___E:Southwest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwestern_United_States)___ before ending in Mexico.

The marriage between Luisa de Abrego, a free Black domestic servant from ___E:Seville U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seville)___ , and Miguel Rodríguez, a White ___E:Segovian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Segovia)___ conquistador in 1565 in ___E:St. Augustine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Augustine,_Florida)___ (Spanish Florida), is the first known and recorded Christian marriage anywhere in what is now the continental United States.

The first recorded Africans in ___E:English America U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_America)___ (including most of the future United States) were ___E:"20 and odd negroes" U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Africans_in_Virginia)___ who arrived in ___E:Jamestown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamestown,_Virginia)___ , ___E:Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colony_of_Virginia)___ via ___E:Cape Comfort U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Point_Comfort)___ in August 1619 as ___E:indentured servants U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indentured_servant)___ .
As many Virginian settlers began to die from harsh conditions, more and more Africans were brought to work as laborers.
An indentured servant (who could be White or Black) would work for several years (usually four to seven) without wages.
The status of indentured servants in early Virginia and Maryland was similar to slavery.

Servants could be bought, sold, or leased, and they could be physically beaten for disobedience or attempting to running away. Unlike slaves, they were freed after their term of service expired or if their freedom was purchased.

Their children did not inherit their status, and on their release from contract they received "a year's provision of corn, double apparel, tools necessary", and a small cash payment called "freedom dues".
Africans could legally raise crops and cattle to purchase their freedom.

They raised families, married other Africans and sometimes ___E:intermarried U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interracial_marriage)___ with Native Americans or European ___E:settlers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Settler)___ .

By the 1640s and 1650s, several African families owned farms around ___E:Jamestown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamestown,_Virginia)___ , and some became wealthy by colonial standards and purchased indentured servants of their own. In 1640, the Virginia General Court recorded the earliest documentation of lifetime slavery when they sentenced ___E:John Punch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Punch_(slave))___ , a Negro, to lifetime servitude under his master ___E:Hugh Gwyn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Gwyn)___ , for running away.

In ___E:Spanish Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Florida)___ , some ___E:Spanish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spaniards)___ married or had ___E:unions with U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Placage)___ ___E:Pensacola U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola_people)___ , ___E:Creek U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscogee)___ or ___E:African U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ethnic_groups_of_Africa)___ women, both enslaved and free, and their descendants created a mixed-race population of ___E:mestizos U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mestizo)___ and ___E:mulattos U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mulatto)___ .

The Spanish encouraged slaves from the ___E:colony of Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_Georgia)___ to come to Florida as a refuge, promising freedom in exchange for conversion to ___E:Catholicism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church)___ . ___E:King Charles II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_II_of_Spain)___ issued a royal proclamation freeing all slaves who fled to Spanish Florida and accepted conversion and baptism.
Most went to the area around ___E:St. Augustine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Augustine,_Florida)___ , but escaped slaves also reached Pensacola.
St. Augustine had mustered an all-Black ___E:militia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Militia)___ unit defending Spanish Florida as early as 1683.

One of the Dutch African arrivals, ___E:Anthony Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Johnson_(American_Colonial))___ , would later own one of the first Black "slaves", ___E:John Casor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Casor)___ , resulting from the court ruling of a civil case.
The popular conception of a race-based slave system did not fully develop until the 18th century.

The ___E:Dutch West India Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_West_India_Company)___ introduced slavery in 1625 with the importation of eleven Black slaves into ___E:New Amsterdam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Amsterdam)___ (present-day New York City).
All the colony's slaves, however, were freed upon its surrender to the English.

___E:Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Bay_Colony)___ was the first English colony to legally recognize slavery in 1641. In 1662, Virginia passed a law that children of enslaved women would take the status of the mother, rather than that of the father, as was the case under ___E:common law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_law)___ .
This legal principle was called partus sequitur ventrum .
By an act of 1699, Virginia ordered the deportation of all free Blacks, effectively defining all people of African descent who remained in the colony as slaves.

In 1670, the colonial assembly passed a law prohibiting free and baptized Blacks (and Native Americans) from purchasing Christians (in this act meaning White Europeans) but allowing them to buy people "of their owne nation".

In ___E:Spanish Louisiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_(New_Spain))___ , although there was no movement toward abolition of the African slave trade, Spanish rule introduced a new law called ___E:coartación U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coartaci%C3%B3n_(slavery))___ , which allowed slaves to buy their freedom, and that of others.
Although some did not have the money to do so, government measures on slavery enabled the existence of many free Blacks.

This caused problems to the Spaniards with the ___E:French creoles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_creoles)___ (French who had settled in ___E:New France U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_France)___ ) who had also populated Spanish Louisiana.
The French creoles cited that measure as one of the system's worst elements.
First established in South Carolina in 1704, groups of armed White men— ___E:slave patrols U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slave_patrol)___ —were formed to monitor enslaved Black people.
Their function was to police slaves, especially fugitives.

Slave owners feared that slaves might organize revolts or ___E:slave rebellions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slave_rebellion)___ , so state militias were formed to provide a military command structure and discipline within the slave patrols.
These patrols were used to detect, encounter, and crush any organized slave meetings which might lead to revolts or ___E:rebellions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebellion)___ .

The earliest African American congregations and churches were organized before 1800 in both northern and southern cities following the ___E:Great Awakening U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Great_Awakening)___ .

By 1775, Africans made up 20% of the population in the ___E:American colonies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteen_Colonies)___ , which made them the second largest ethnic group after ___E:English Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Americans)___ .

During the 1770s, Africans, both enslaved and free, helped rebellious American colonists secure their independence by defeating the British in the ___E:American Revolutionary War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolutionary_War)___ .
Blacks played a role in both sides in the American Revolution.

Activists in the Patriot cause included ___E:James Armistead U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Armistead)___ , ___E:Prince Whipple U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Whipple)___ , and ___E:Oliver Cromwell U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Cromwell_(American_soldier))___ .

Around 15,000 ___E:Black Loyalists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Loyalist)___ left with the British after the war, most of them ending up as free Black people in England  or its colonies, such as the ___E:Black Nova Scotians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Nova_Scotians)___ and the ___E:Sierra Leone Creole people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Leone_Creole_people)___ .

In the ___E:Spanish Louisiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Louisiana)___ , Governor ___E:Bernardo de Gálvez U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernardo_de_G%C3%A1lvez)___ organized Spanish free Black men into two militia companies to defend ___E:New Orleans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans)___ during the American Revolution.
They fought in the 1779 battle in which Spain captured ___E:Baton Rouge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baton_Rouge)___ from the British.

Gálvez also commanded them in campaigns against the British outposts in ___E:Mobile U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile,_Alabama)___ , ___E:Alabama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama)___ , and ___E:Pensacola U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola)___ , Florida.

He recruited slaves for the militia by pledging to free anyone who was seriously wounded and promised to secure a low price for coartación (buy their freedom and that of others) for those who received lesser wounds.

During the 1790s, Governor ___E:Francisco Luis Héctor, baron of Carondelet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Luis_H%C3%A9ctor_de_Carondelet)___ reinforced local fortifications and recruit even more free Black men for the militia.

Carondelet doubled the number of free Black men who served, creating two more militia companies—one made up of Black members and the other of ___E:pardo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pardo)___ (mixed race).
Serving in the militia brought free Black men one step closer to equality with Whites, allowing them, for example, the right to carry arms and boosting their earning power.
However, actually these privileges distanced free Black men from enslaved Blacks and encouraged them to identify with Whites.

Slavery had been tacitly enshrined in the ___E:US Constitution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Constitution)___ through provisions such as Article I, Section 2, Clause 3, commonly known as the ___E:3/5 compromise U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3/5_compromise)___ .

Due to the restrictions of ___E:Section 9, Clause 1 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Article_One_of_the_United_States_Constitution#Clause_1:_Slave_trade)___ , Congress was unable to pass an ___E:Act Prohibiting Importation of Slaves U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Act_Prohibiting_Importation_of_Slaves)___ until 1807.  ___E:Fugitive slave laws U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_slave_laws_in_the_United_States)___ (derived from the ___E:Fugitive Slave Clause U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Slave_Clause)___ of the Constitution— ___E:Article IV, Section 2, Clause 3 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Article_Four_of_the_United_States_Constitution#Clause_3:_Fugitive_Slave_Clause)___ ) were passed by Congress in both ___E:1793 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Slave_Act_of_1793)___ and ___E:1850 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Slave_Act_of_1850)___ , guaranteeing the right of a slaveholder to recover an escaped slave anywhere within the US.  Slave owners, who viewed enslaved people as property, ensured that it became a federal crime to aid or assist those who had fled slavery or to interfere with their capture.

By that time, slavery, which almost exclusively targeted Black people, had become the most critical and contentious political issue in the ___E:Antebellum United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antebellum_United_States)___ , repeatedly sparking crises and conflicts.

Among these were the ___E:Missouri Compromise U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Compromise)___ , the ___E:Compromise of 1850 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compromise_of_1850)___ , the infamous ___E:Dred Scott decision U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dred_Scott_decision)___ , and ___E:John Brown's raid on Harpers Ferry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Brown%27s_raid_on_Harpers_Ferry)___ .
Prior to the ___E:Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War)___ , eight serving presidents had owned slaves, a practice that was legally protected under the US Constitution.

By 1860, the number of enslaved Black people in the US had grown to between 3.5 and 4.4 million, largely as a result of the ___E:Atlantic slave trade U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_slave_trade)___ .
In addition, 488,000–500,000 Black people lived free (with legislated limits)  across the country.
With legislated limits imposed upon them in addition to "unconquerable prejudice" from Whites according to ___E:Henry Clay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay)___ .
In response to these conditions, some free Black people chose to leave the US and emigrate to ___E:Liberia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberia)___ in West Africa.

Liberia had been established in 1821 as a settlement by the ___E:American Colonization Society U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Colonization_Society)___ (ACS), with many abolitionist members of the ACS believing Black Americans would have greater opportunities for freedom and equality in Africa than they would in the US.

Slaves not only represented a significant financial investment for their owners, but they also played a crucial role in producing the country's most valuable product and export: ___E:cotton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Cotton)___ .

Enslaved people were instrumental in the construction of several prominent structures such as, the ___E:United States Capitol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Capitol)___ , the ___E:White House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House)___ and other ___E:Washington, D.C.–based U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_in_the_District_of_Columbia)___ buildings.
Similar building projects existed in the ___E:slave states U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slave_states_and_free_states)___ .

By 1815, the ___E:domestic slave trade U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_in_the_United_States#Domestic_slave_trade_and_forced_migration)___ had become a significant and major economic activity in the United States, continuing to flourish until the 1860s.
Historians estimate that nearly one million individuals were subjected to this forced migration, which was often referred to as a new "Middle Passage".

The historian ___E:Ira Berlin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ira_Berlin)___ described this internal forced migration of enslaved people as the "central event" in the life of a slave during the period between the American Revolution and the Civil War. Berlin emphasized that whether enslaved individuals were directly uprooted or lived in constant fear that they or their families would be involuntarily relocated, "the massive deportation traumatized Black people" throughout the US.  As a result of this large-scale forced movement, countless individuals lost their connection to families and clans, and many ethnic Africans lost their knowledge of varying tribal origins in Africa.

The 1863 photograph of ___E:Wilson Chinn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilson_Chinn)___ , a branded slave from Louisiana, along with the famous image of ___E:Gordon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_(slave))___ and his scarred back, served as two of the earliest and most powerful examples of how the newborn medium of photography could be used to visually document and encapsulate the brutality and cruelty of slavery.

Emigration of free Blacks to their continent of origin had been proposed since the Revolutionary war. After ___E:Haiti U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiti)___ became independent, it tried to recruit African Americans to migrate there after it re-established trade relations with the United States.
The Haitian Union was a group formed to promote relations between the countries.

After riots against Blacks in ___E:Cincinnati U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati)___ , its Black community sponsored founding of the ___E:Wilberforce Colony U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilberforce_Colony)___ , an initially successful settlement of African American immigrants to Canada.
The colony was one of the first such independent political entities.
It lasted for a number of decades and provided a destination for about 200 Black families emigrating from a number of locations in the United States.

In 1863, during the ___E:American Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War)___ , President ___E:Abraham Lincoln U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln)___ signed the ___E:Emancipation Proclamation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emancipation_Proclamation)___ .
The proclamation declared that all slaves in Confederate-held territory were free.  Advancing Union troops enforced the proclamation, with Texas being the last state to be emancipated, in 1865.

Slavery in a few border states continued until the ratification of the ___E:Thirteenth Amendment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution)___ in December 1865.  While the ___E:Naturalization Act of 1790 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naturalization_Act_of_1790)___ limited US citizenship to Whites only,   the ___E:14th Amendment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution)___ (1868) gave Black people citizenship, and the ___E:15th Amendment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution)___ (1870) gave Black men the right to vote.
African Americans quickly set up congregations for themselves, as well as schools and community/civic associations, to have space away from White control or oversight.

While the post-war Reconstruction era was initially a time of progress for African Americans, that period ended in 1876. By the late 1890s, Southern states enacted Jim Crow laws to enforce ___E:racial segregation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_segregation)___ and ___E:disenfranchisement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disfranchisement_after_the_American_Civil_War)___ .

Segregation was now imposed with Jim Crow laws, using signs used to show Blacks where they could legally walk, talk, drink, rest, or eat.  For those places that were racially mixed, non-Whites had to wait until all White customers were dealt with.  Most African Americans obeyed the Jim Crow laws, to avoid ___E:racially motivated violence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnic_violence)___ .

To maintain self-esteem and dignity, African Americans such as ___E:Anthony Overton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Overton)___ and ___E:Mary McLeod Bethune U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_McLeod_Bethune)___ continued to build their own ___E:schools U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historically_Black_colleges_and_universities)___ , ___E:churches U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_church)___ , banks, social clubs, and other businesses.

State governments soon moved to undermine their citizenship by restricting their right to vote. By the late 1870s, Blacks were disenfranchised and segregated across the American South.
White politicians in Mississippi and other states withheld financial resources and supplies from Black schools.

Nevertheless, the presence of Black teachers, and their engagement with their communities both inside and outside the classroom, ensured that Black students had access to education despite these external constraints.

At the close of the war, Chicago's Board of Education downgraded the curriculum's status from mandatory to optional.

Separating this statistic into component parts shows it varies greatly depending upon the state and the school district examined. 38% of Black males graduated in the state of New York but in Maine 97% graduated and exceeded the White male graduation rate by 11 percentage points.

In much of the southeastern United States and some parts of the southwestern United States the graduation rate of White males was in fact below 70% such as in Florida where 62% of White males graduated from high school.
Examining specific school districts paints an even more complex picture.
In the Detroit school district, the graduation rate of Black males was 20% but 7% for White males.
In the New York City school district 28% of Black males graduate from high school compared to 57% of White males.
In Newark County [where?] 76% of Black males graduated compared to 67% for White males.
Further academic improvement has occurred in 2015. Roughly 23% of all Blacks have bachelor's degrees.
In 1988, 21% of Whites had obtained a bachelor's degree versus 11% of Blacks.
In 2015, 23% of Blacks had obtained a bachelor's degree versus 36% of Whites.
Foreign born Blacks, 9% of the Black population, made even greater strides.
They exceed native born Blacks by 10 percentage points.

___E:College Board U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_Board)___ , which runs the official college-level ___E:advanced placement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advanced_Placement)___ (AP) programs in American high schools, have has received criticism in recent years that its curricula have focused too much on ___E:Euro-centric U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro-centric)___ history.

According to a 2025 study, African Americans have the highest average ___E:student debt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Student_loans_in_the_United_States)___ .
African Americans with ___E:bachelor's degrees U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor%27s_degrees)___ owe an average of $52,726 in student loans.
Nearly 70% of African Americans took out a loan to fund their undergraduate education.

Historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs), which were founded when ___E:segregated institutions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_segregation_in_the_United_States)___ of higher learning did not admit African Americans, continue to thrive and educate students of all races today.

There are 101 HBCUs representing three percent of the nation's colleges and universities with the majority established in the ___E:Southeast U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_United_States)___ .
HBCUs have been largely responsible for establishing and expanding the African American middle-class by providing more career opportunities for African Americans.
The economic disparity between the races in the US has marginally improved since the end of slavery.

Poverty is associated with higher rates of marital stress and dissolution, ___E:physical U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_disorder)___ and ___E:mental health U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_disorder)___ problems, ___E:disability U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disability_and_poverty)___ , ___E:cognitive deficits U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_deficit)___ , ___E:low educational attainment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achievement_gap_in_the_United_States)___ , and crime.
African Americans have a long and diverse history of business ownership.

Although the first African American business is unknown, slaves captured from West Africa are believed to have established commercial enterprises as peddlers and skilled craftspeople as far back as the 17th century.
Around 1900, Booker T. Washington became the most famous proponent of African American businesses.
His critic and rival W. E.
B. DuBois also commended business as a vehicle for African American advancement.

African Americans had a combined buying power of over $1.6 trillion as of 2021, a 171% increase of their buying power in 2000 but lagging significantly in growth behind American ___E:Latinos U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans)___ and ___E:Asians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Americans)___ in the same timer period (with 288% and 383%, respectively; for reference, US growth overall was 144% in the same period); however, African American net worth had shrunk 14% in the previous year despite strong growth in property prices and the ___E:S&P 500 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%26P_500)___ .
In 2002, African American-owned businesses accounted for 1.2 million of the US's 23 million businesses.
As of 2011 [update] , African American-owned businesses account for approximately 2 million ___E:US businesses U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_businesses)___ .
Black-owned businesses experienced the largest growth in number of businesses among minorities from 2002 to 2011.

Twenty-five percent of Blacks had ___E:white-collar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White-collar_worker)___ occupations (management, professional, and related fields) in 2000, compared with 33.6% of Americans overall.

In 2001, over half of African American households of married couples earned $50,000 or more.  Although in the same year African Americans were over-represented among the nation's poor, this was directly related to the disproportionate percentage of African American families headed by single women; such families are collectively poorer, regardless of ethnicity.
In 2006, the median earnings of African American men was more than Black and non-Black American women overall, and in all educational levels.

At the same time, among American men, income disparities were significant; the median income of African American men was approximately 76 cents for every dollar of their European American counterparts, although the gap narrowed somewhat with a rise in educational level.

Overall, the median earnings of African American men were 72 cents for every dollar earned of their Asian American counterparts, and $1.17 for every dollar earned by Hispanic men.    On the other hand, by 2006, among American women with post-secondary education, African American women have made significant advances; the median income of African American women was more than those of their Asian-, European- and Hispanic American counterparts with at least some college education.
The US ___E:public sector U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_sector)___ is the single most important source of employment for African Americans.
During 2008–2010, 21.2% of all Black workers were public employees, compared with 16.3% of non-Black workers.

Both before and after the onset of the ___E:Great Recession U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Recession)___ , African Americans were 30% more likely than other workers to be employed in the public sector.
The public sector is also a critical source of decent-paying jobs for Black Americans.
For both men and women, the median wage earned by Black employees is significantly higher in the public sector than in other industries.
In 1999, the median income of African American families was $33,255 compared to $53,356 of European Americans.

In times of economic hardship for the nation, African Americans suffer disproportionately from job loss and ___E:underemployment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underemployment)___ , with the Black underclass being hardest hit. The phrase "last hired and first fired" is reflected in the ___E:Bureau of Labor Statistics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Labor_Statistics)___ unemployment figures.
Nationwide, the October 2008 unemployment rate for African Americans was 11.1%,  while the nationwide rate was 6.5%.
In 2007, the average income for African Americans was approximately $34,000, compared to $55,000 for Whites.
African Americans experience a higher rate of unemployment than the general population.
The income gap between Black and White families is also significant.

In 2005, employed Blacks earned 65% of the wages of Whites, down from 82% in 1975.  The New York Times reported in 2006 that in ___E:Queens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens)___ , New York, the median income among African American families exceeded that of White families, which the newspaper attributed to the growth in the number of two-parent Black families.

It noted that Queens was the only county with more than 65,000 residents where that was true.  In 2011, it was reported that ___E:72% of Black babies were born to unwed mothers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_family_structure)___ .

The poverty rate among single-parent Black families was 39.5% in 2005, according to ___E:Walter E. Williams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_E._Williams)___ , while it was 9.9% among married-couple Black families.
Among White families, the respective rates were 26.4% and 6% in poverty.

Collectively, African Americans are more involved in the American political process than other minority groups in the United States, indicated by the highest level of voter registration and participation in elections among these groups in 2004.  African Americans also have the highest level of ___E:Congressional representation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress)___ of any minority group in the US.

___E:Homeownership in the US U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home-ownership_in_the_United_States)___ is the strongest indicator of financial stability and the primary asset most Americans use to generate wealth.
African Americans continue to lag behind other racial groups in homeownership.
In the first quarter of 2021, 45.1% of African Americans owned their homes, compared to 65.3% of all Americans.

The African American homeownership rate has remained relatively flat since the 1970s despite an increase in ___E:anti-discrimination housing laws and protections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Housing_discrimination_in_the_United_States)___ .
The African American homeownership rate peaked in 2004 at 49.7%.

The average White high school drop-out still has a slightly better chance of owning a home than the average African American college graduate usually due to unfavorable ___E:debt-to-income ratios U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debt-to-income_ratio)___ or ___E:credit scores U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Credit_score_in_the_United_States)___ among most African American college graduates.

Since 2000, fast-growing housing costs in most cities have made it even more difficult for the US African American homeownership rate to significantly grow and reach over 50% for the first time in history.

From 2000 to 2022, the median home price in the US grew 160%, outpacing average annual household income growth in that same period, which only grew about 30%.    ___E:South Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina)___ is the state with the most African American homeownership, with about 55% of African Americans owning their own homes.
Black people, who make up 12% of the total U.S. population, make up 32% of all people experiencing homelessness, according to the data.
Since the mid 20th century, a large majority of African Americans support the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ .

In the ___E:2024 Presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election)___ , 86% of African American voters supported Democrat ___E:Kamala Harris U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris)___ , while 13% supported Republican ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ .
Although there is an African American lobby in foreign policy, it has not had the impact that African American organizations have had in domestic policy.
Many African Americans were excluded from electoral politics in the decades following the end of Reconstruction.

For those that could participate, until the ___E:New Deal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Deal)___ , African Americans were supporters of the Republican Party because it was Republican President Abraham Lincoln who helped in granting freedom to American slaves; at the time, the Republicans and Democrats represented the ___E:sectional U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sectionalism)___ interests of the ___E:North U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_United_States)___ and ___E:South U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_United_States)___ , respectively, rather than any specific ideology, and both ___E:conservative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatism_in_the_United_States)___ and ___E:liberal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_liberalism_in_the_United_States)___ were represented equally in both parties.

The African American trend of voting for Democrats can be traced back to the 1930s during the ___E:Great Depression U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression)___ , when ___E:Franklin D. Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt)___ 's ___E:New Deal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Deal)___ program provided economic relief to African Americans.

Roosevelt's ___E:New Deal coalition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Deal_coalition)___ turned the Democratic Party into an organization of the working class and their liberal allies, regardless of region.

The African American vote became even more solidly Democratic when Democratic presidents ___E:John F. Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy)___ and ___E:Lyndon B. Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson)___ pushed for civil rights legislation during the 1960s.
In 1960, nearly a third of African Americans voted for Republican ___E:Richard Nixon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon)___ .
___E:Conservatism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatism)___ has been steadily growing among African Americans, particularly since the 2020 Presidential election.
In the 2024 election, Trump secured a larger share of the African American vote compared to his 2020 performance.

Notably, Black men and younger Black voters have increasingly aligned with the ___E:Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ , adopting more conservative stances, such as supporting stricter crime policies, placing less emphasis on ___E:transgender rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender_rights_movement)___ , and advocating for an end to ___E:illegal immigration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illegal_immigration)___ , which marks a shift from the views of previous generations.
" ___E:Lift Every Voice and Sing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lift_Every_Voice_and_Sing)___ " is often referred to as the Black national anthem in the United States.

In 1919, the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) had dubbed it the "Negro national anthem" for its power in voicing a cry for liberation and affirmation for African-American people.
The majority of African Americans are ___E:Protestant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestant)___ , many of whom follow the historically Black churches.

One of these early African American Christian cultural traditions in the Black Church is the ___E:Watchnight service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watchnight_service)___ , also called Freedom's Eve, where African American congregations all over the nation come together on New Year's Eve through New Years morning in remembrance of the eve and New Year of their emancipation, sharing testimonies, being baptized and partaking in praise and worship.
According to a 2007 survey, more than half of the African American population are part of the historically Black churches.

The largest Protestant denomination among African Americans are the ___E:Baptists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptists)___ ,  distributed mainly in four denominations, the largest being the ___E:National Baptist Convention, USA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Baptist_Convention,_USA,_Inc.)___ and the ___E:National Baptist Convention of America U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Baptist_Convention_of_America,_Inc.)___ .

The second largest are the ___E:Methodists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methodist)___ ,  the largest denominations are the ___E:African Methodist Episcopal Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Methodist_Episcopal_Church)___ and the ___E:African Methodist Episcopal Zion Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Methodist_Episcopal_Zion_Church)___ .

___E:African American Muslims U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_Muslims)___ constitute 20% of the total ___E:US Muslim population U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam_in_the_United_States)___ ,  the majority are ___E:Sunni U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunni_Islam)___ or orthodox Muslims, some of these identify under the community of ___E:W. The life expectancy for Black men in 2008 was 70.8 years.

Life expectancy for Black women was 77.5 years in 2008.  In 1900, when information on Black life expectancy started being collated, a Black man could expect to live to 32.5 years and a Black woman 33.5 years.

African American life expectancy at birth is persistently five to seven years lower than ___E:European Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Americans)___ .

African Americans have several ___E:barriers for accessing mental health U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obstacles_to_receiving_mental_health_services_among_African_American_youth)___ services. ___E:Counseling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_health_counselor)___ has been frowned upon and distant in utility and proximity to many people in the African American community.
In 2004, a qualitative research study explored the disconnect with African Americans and mental health.
The study was conducted as a semi-structured discussion which allowed the focus group to express their opinions and life experiences.

The results revealed a couple key variables that create barriers for many African American communities to seek mental health services such as the stigma, lack of four important necessities; trust, affordability, cultural understanding and impersonal services.
Historically, many African American communities did not seek counseling because religion was a part of the family values.
African American who have a faith background are more likely to seek prayer as a coping mechanism for mental issues rather than seeking professional mental health services.
In 2015 a study concluded, African Americans with high value in religion are less likely to utilize mental health services compared to those who have low value in religion.

In the United States, counseling approaches are based on the experience of ___E:White Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Americans)___ and do not fit within the African American culture.
African American families tend to resolve concerns within the family, and it is viewed by the family as a strength.
On the other hand, when African Americans seek counseling, they face a social backlash and are criticized.
They may be labeled "crazy", viewed as weak, and their pride is diminished.
Because of this, many African Americans instead seek mentorship within communities they trust.
Terminology is another barrier in relation to African Americans and mental health.
There is more stigma on the term psychotherapy versus counseling.

In one study, psychotherapy is associated with mental illness whereas counseling approaches problem-solving, guidance and help.  More African Americans seek assistance when it is called counseling and not psychotherapy because it is more welcoming within the cultural and community.
Counselors are encouraged to be aware of such barriers for the well-being of African American clients.
Without ___E:cultural competency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_competence_in_healthcare)___ training in health care, many African Americans go unheard and misunderstood.
In 2021, African Americans had the third highest ___E:suicide U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicide)___ rate trailing American Indians/Alaska Natives and White Americans.

Recent studies of African Americans using genetic testing have found ancestry to vary by region and sex of ancestors.
These studies found that on average, African Americans have 73.2–82.1% Sub-Saharan African, 16.7–24% European, and 0.8–1.2% Native American genetic ancestry, with large variation between individuals.
Commercial testing services have reported similar variation, with ranges from 0.6 to 2 percent Native American, 19 to 29 percent European, and 65 to 80 percent Sub-Saharan African ancestry.

According to a genome-wide study by Bryc et al. (2009), the mixed ancestry of African Americans in varying ratios came about as the result of sexual contact between West/Central Africans (more frequently females) and Europeans (more frequently males).

This can be understood as being the result of enslaved African American females being ___E:raped U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_sexual_slavery_in_the_United_States#Under_chattel_slavery)___ by White males.

Consequently, the 365 African Americans in their sample have a genome-wide average of 78.1% West African ancestry and 18.5% European ancestry, with large variation among individuals (ranging from 99% to 1% West African ancestry).

The West African ancestral component in African Americans is most similar to that in present-day speakers from the non- ___E:Bantu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_languages)___ branches of the ___E:Niger-Congo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niger-Congo_languages)___ family.  [note 2]

Correspondingly, Montinaro et al. (2014) observed that around 50% of the overall ancestry of African Americans traces comes from a population similar to the Niger-Congo-speaking ___E:Yoruba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoruba_people)___ of southern ___E:Nigeria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria)___ and southern ___E:Benin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benin)___ , reflecting the centrality of this West African region in the Atlantic slave trade.
The next most frequent ancestral component found among African Americans was derived from Great Britain, in keeping with historical records.

It constitutes a little over 10% of their overall ancestry and is most similar to the Northwest European ancestral component also carried by ___E:Barbadians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbadians)___ .

Zakharia et al. (2009) found a similar proportion of Yoruba-like ancestry in their African American samples, with a minority also drawn from ___E:Mandenka U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandinka_people)___ and ___E:Bantu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_peoples)___ populations.
Additionally, the researchers observed an average European ancestry of 21.9%, again with significant variation between individuals.

Bryc et al. (2009) note that populations from other parts of the continent may also constitute adequate proxies for the ancestors of some African American individuals; namely, ancestral populations from ___E:Guinea Bissau U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinea_Bissau)___ , ___E:Senegal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senegal)___ and ___E:Sierra Leone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Leone)___ in West Africa and ___E:Angola U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angola)___ in Southern Africa.
An individual African American person can have over fifteen African ethnic groups in their genetic makeup alone due to the slave trade covering such vast areas.
Altogether, genetic studies suggest that African Americans are a genetically diverse people.

According to DNA analysis led in 2006 by ___E:Penn State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania_State_University)___ geneticist ___E:Mark D. Shriver U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_D._Shriver)___ , around 58 percent of African Americans have at least 12.5% European ancestry (equivalent to one European great-grandparent and their forebears), 19.6 percent of African Americans have at least 25% European ancestry (equivalent to one European grandparent and their forebears), and 1 percent of African Americans have at least 50% European ancestry (equivalent to one European parent and their forebears).
According to Shriver, around 5 percent of African Americans also have at least 12.5% Native American ancestry (equivalent to one Native American great-grandparent and their forebears).

Research suggests that Native American ancestry among people who identify as African American is a result of relationships that occurred soon after slave ships arrived in the American colonies, and European ancestry is of more recent origin, often from the decades before the Civil War.

Africans bearing the ___E:E-V38 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haplogroup_E-V38)___ (E1b1a) likely traversed across the ___E:Sahara U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahara)___ , from ___E:east U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa)___ to ___E:west U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Africa)___ , approximately 19,000 years ago.  ___E:E-M2 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haplogroup_E-M2)___ (E1b1a1) likely originated in West Africa or Central Africa.

According to a ___E:Y-DNA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y_chromosome)___ study by Sims et al. (2007), the majority (≈60%) of African Americans belong to various subclades of the ___E:E-M2 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haplogroup_E-M2)___ (E1b1a1, formerly E3a) paternal haplogroup.

This is the most common genetic paternal lineage found today among West/Central African males and is also a signature of the historical ___E:Bantu migrations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_migration)___ .

The next most frequent Y-DNA haplogroup observed among African Americans is the ___E:R1b U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haplogroup_R1b_(Y-DNA))___ clade, which around 15% of African Americans carry.
This lineage is most common today among Northwestern European males.
The remaining African Americans mainly belong to the paternal ___E:haplogroup I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haplogroup_I-M170)___ (≈7%), which is also frequent in Northwestern Europe.

According to an ___E:mtDNA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitochondrial_DNA)___ study by Salas et al. (2005), the maternal lineages of African Americans are most similar to haplogroups that are today especially common in West Africa (>55%), followed closely by West-Central Africa and Southwestern Africa (<41%).

The characteristic West African haplogroups ___E:L1b U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haplogroup_L1_(mtDNA))___ , ___E:L2b,c,d U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haplogroup_L2_(mtDNA))___ , and ___E:L3b,d U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haplogroup_L3_(mtDNA))___ and West-Central African haplogroups ___E:L1c U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haplogroup_L1_(mtDNA))___ and ___E:L3e U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haplogroup_L3_(mtDNA))___ in particular occur at high frequencies among African Americans.
As with the paternal DNA of African Americans, contributions from other parts of the continent to their maternal gene pool are insignificant.
Formal political, economic and social discrimination against minorities has been present throughout American history.

Leland T. Saito, Associate Professor of Sociology and American Studies & Ethnicity at the ___E:University of Southern California U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Southern_California)___ , writes, "Political rights have been circumscribed by race, class and gender since the founding of the United States, when the right to vote was restricted to White men of property.
Throughout the history of the United States, race has been used by Whites for legitimizing and creating difference and social, economic and political exclusion."

Those who economically gained the most from slavery were the ___E:planter class U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planter_class)___ , owners of large-scale plantations where large numbers of enslaved Africans were held captive and forced to produce crops to create wealth for a White elite.

Having a prominent role in politics with eight presidents owning slaves while in office, upon the end of the Civil War the planter class kept control of their land and remained politically influential, with the ___E:London School of Economics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_School_of_Economics)___ stating, "this persistence in "de facto power" in turn allowed them to block economic reforms, disenfranchise Black voters, and restrict the mobility of workers."

Although they have gained a greater degree of social equality since the civil rights movement, African Americans have remained stagnant economically, which has hindered their ability to break into the middle class and beyond.

As of 2020, the ___E:racial wealth gap U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_inequality_in_the_United_States)___ between Whites and Blacks remains as large as it was in 1968, with the typical net worth of a White household equivalent to that of 11.5 Black households.

Despite this, African Americans have increased employment rates and gained representation in the highest levels of American government in the post–civil rights era.  However, widespread ___E:racism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racism_against_African_Americans)___ remains an issue that continues to undermine the development of social status.
Economically, of all the racially Black ethnic groups on the globe, African Americans are the wealthiest and most successful, with one in every fifty African American families being millionaires.

This equates in 2023 to approximately 1.79 million African American millionaires in the United States,   which is more than the total amount of millionaires in any racially Black country, and many other countries, around the world.

In the US, which has the largest per-capita prison population in the world, African Americans are overrepresented as the second largest population of prison inmates (38%) in 2023, coming second to Whites who made up 57% of the prison population.

According to the ___E:National Registry of Exonerations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Registry_of_Exonerations)___ , Blacks are roughly 7.5 times more likely to be wrongfully convicted of murder in the US than Whites.

In 2012, the New York City Police Department detained people more than 500,000 times under the city's ___E:stop-and-frisk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop-and-frisk)___ law. Of the total detained, 55% were African-Americans, while Black people made up 20% of the city's population.
African American males are more likely to be ___E:killed by police U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_use_of_deadly_force_in_the_United_States)___ when compared to other races.

This is one of the factors that led to the creation of the ___E:Black Lives Matter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Lives_Matter)___ movement in 2013.  A historical issue in the US where women have weaponized their White privilege in the country by reporting on Black people, often instigating racial violence,   difficult White women—who have been given a ___E:different name over the centuries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen_(slang)#Origin)___ by African Americans—calling the police on Black people became widely publicized in 2020.   According to The Guardian , "The specter of ___E:Karen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen_(slang))___ persisted as Black Lives Matter protests and civil unrest spread around the country following ___E:Floyd's murder U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_of_George_Floyd)___ and reckonings with racism began to roil institutions, toppling careers as well as statues".
In the aftermath of the peak Black Lives Matter protests and widespread police reform efforts, crime rates surged across the nation.
Many cities experienced near-record or record levels of violence and other criminal activity.
As a result, numerous municipalities scaled back police reform initiatives and increased funding for law enforcement.
After over 50 years, marriage rates for all Americans began to decline while divorce rates and out-of-wedlock births have climbed.
These changes have been greatest among African Americans.

After more than 70 years of racial parity Black marriage rates began to fall behind Whites.  ___E:Single-parent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_parents_in_the_United_States)___ households have become common, and according to US census figures released in January 2010, only 38 percent of Black children live with both their parents.
In 2021, statistics show that over 80 percent marriages in the African American ethnic group marry within their ethnic group.

The first ever ___E:anti-miscegenation law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-miscegenation_law)___ was passed by the ___E:Maryland General Assembly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland_General_Assembly)___ in 1691, criminalizing ___E:interracial marriage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interracial_marriage)___ .

In a speech in ___E:Charleston, Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charleston,_Illinois)___ in 1858, ___E:Abraham Lincoln U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln)___ stated, "I am not, nor ever have been in favor of making voters or jurors of negroes, nor of qualifying them to hold office, nor to intermarry with white people".
By the late 1800s, 38 US states had anti-miscegenation statutes.
By 1924, the ban on interracial marriage was still in force in 29 states.

While interracial marriage had been legal in California since 1948, in 1957 actor ___E:Sammy Davis Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sammy_Davis_Jr.)___ faced a backlash for his involvement with White actress ___E:Kim Novak U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Novak)___ .  ___E:Harry Cohn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Cohn)___ , the president of Columbia Pictures, with whom Novak was under contract, gave in to his concerns that a racist backlash against the relationship could hurt the studio.
Davis briefly married Black dancer Loray White in 1958 to protect himself from mob violence.

Inebriated at the wedding ceremony, Davis despairingly said to his best friend, Arthur Silber Jr., "Why won't they let me live my life?" The couple never lived together, and commenced divorce proceedings in September 1958.  In 1958, officers in ___E:Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia)___ entered the home of ___E:Mildred and Richard Loving U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loving_v._Virginia#Plaintiffs)___ and dragged them out of bed for living together as an interracial couple, on the basis that "any white person intermarry with a colored person"—or vice versa—each party "shall be guilty of a felony" and face prison terms of five years.

In 1967 the law was ruled unconstitutional (via the ___E:14th Amendment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution)___ adopted in 1868) by the US Supreme Court in Loving v. Virginia .

In 2008, Democrats overwhelmingly voted 70% against ___E:California Proposition 8 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Proposition_8)___ , African Americans voted 58% in favor of it while 42% voted against Proposition 8.  On May 9, 2012, Barack Obama, the first Black president, became the first US president to support same-sex marriage.
Since Obama's endorsement there has been a rapid growth in support for same-sex marriage among African Americans.
As of 2012, 59% of African Americans support same-sex marriage, which is higher than support among the national average (53%) and White Americans (50%).

Polls in ___E:North Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina)___ ,  ___E:Pennsylvania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania)___ ,  ___E:Missouri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri)___ ,  ___E:Maryland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland)___ ,  ___E:Ohio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio)___ ,  Florida,  and ___E:Nevada U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada)___  have also shown an increase in support for same sex marriage among African Americans.

On November 6, 2012, ___E:Maryland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland_Question_6)___ , ___E:Maine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Question_1,_2012)___ , and ___E:Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Referendum_74)___ all voted for approve of same-sex marriage, along with Minnesota rejecting a ___E:constitutional amendment banning same-sex marriage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Amendment_1)___ .

Exit polls in Maryland show about 50% of African Americans voted for same-sex marriage, showing a vast evolution among African Americans on the issue and was crucial in helping pass same-sex marriage in Maryland.
Black Americans hold far more conservative opinions on abortion, ___E:extramarital sex U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affair)___ , and raising children out of wedlock than Democrats as a whole.

On financial issues, however, African Americans are in line with Democrats, generally supporting a more ___E:progressive tax U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_tax)___ structure to provide more government spending on social services.

___E:African Americans have fought in every war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_African_Americans)___ in the ___E:history of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_the_United_States)___ .

The gains made by African Americans in the ___E:civil rights movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_rights_movement)___ and in the ___E:Black Power movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Power_movement)___ not only obtained certain rights for African Americans but changed American society in far-reaching and fundamentally important ways. Prior to the 1950s, Black Americans in the South were subject to de jure discrimination, or ___E:Jim Crow laws U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Crow_laws)___ .

They were often the victims of extreme cruelty and violence, sometimes resulting in deaths: by the post World War II era, African Americans became increasingly discontented with their long-standing inequality.

In the words of ___E:Martin Luther King Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther_King_Jr.)___ , African Americans and their supporters challenged the nation to "rise up and live out the true meaning of its creed that all men are created equal ..."

The civil rights movement marked an enormous change in American social, political, economic and civic life. It brought with it ___E:boycotts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boycott)___ , ___E:sit-ins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sit-in)___ , ___E:nonviolent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonviolent)___ demonstrations and marches, court battles, bombings and other violence; prompted worldwide media coverage and intense public debate; forged enduring civic, economic and religious alliances; and disrupted and realigned the nation's two major political parties.
Over time, it has changed in fundamental ways the manner in which Blacks and Whites interact with and relate to one another.

The movement resulted in the removal of codified, de jure racial segregation and discrimination from American life and law, and heavily influenced other groups and movements in struggles for civil rights and social equality within American society, including the ___E:Free Speech Movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Speech_Movement)___ , the ___E:disabled U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disability)___ , the ___E:women's movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminist_movement)___ , and ___E:migrant workers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Migrant_workers)___ .

It also inspired the ___E:Native American rights movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_rights_movement)___ , and in King's 1964 book Why We Can't Wait he wrote the US "was born in genocide when it embraced the doctrine that the original American, the Indian, was an inferior race."

From their earliest presence in North America, African Americans have significantly contributed literature, art, agricultural skills, cuisine, clothing styles, music, language, and social and technological innovation to American culture.

The cultivation and use of many agricultural products in the United States, such as ___E:yams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweet_potato)___ , peanuts, rice, ___E:okra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Okra)___ , ___E:sorghum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorghum)___ , ___E:grits U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grits)___ , ___E:watermelon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watermelon)___ , ___E:indigo dyes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigo_dye)___ , and cotton, can be traced to West African and African American influences.

Notable examples include ___E:George Washington Carver U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington_Carver)___ , who created nearly 500 products from peanuts, sweet potatoes, and pecans.  ___E:Soul food U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_food)___ is a variety of cuisine popular among African Americans.
It is closely related to the ___E:cuisine of the Southern United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuisine_of_the_Southern_United_States)___ .

The descriptive terminology may have originated in the mid-1960s, when soul was a common definer used to describe African American culture (for example, ___E:soul music U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music)___ ).
African Americans were the first peoples in the United States to make fried chicken, along with ___E:Scottish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_people)___ immigrants to the South.

Although the Scottish had been frying chicken before they emigrated, they lacked the spices and flavor that African Americans had used when preparing the meal. The Scottish American settlers therefore adopted the African American method of seasoning chicken.
However, fried chicken was generally a rare meal in the African American community and was usually reserved for special events or celebrations.

___E:African-American English U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_English)___ is a ___E:variety U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_(linguistics))___ ( ___E:dialect U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dialect)___ , ___E:ethnolect U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnolect)___ , and ___E:sociolect U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociolect)___ ) of ___E:American English U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_English)___ , commonly spoken by urban ___E:working-class U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_class)___ and largely ___E:bi-dialectal U:(https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/bidialectal)___ ___E:middle-class U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_class)___ African Americans.

African American English differs from Standard American English (SAE) in certain pronunciation characteristics, tense usage, and grammatical structures, which were derived from West African languages (particularly those belonging to the ___E:Niger–Congo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niger%E2%80%93Congo_languages)___ family).
Virtually all habitual speakers of African American English can understand and communicate in Standard American English.
As with all linguistic forms, AAVE's usage is influenced by various factors, including geographical, educational and socioeconomic background, as well as formality of setting.
Additionally, there are many literary uses of this variety of English, particularly in ___E:African American literature U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_literature)___ .
